summary: The timing skeleton is scan-time FPGA work: the playfield and alphanumerics are fetched in phases keyed on the pixel counter, and motion objects are built one line ahead into double line buffers. The compositor's behavior, though, is defined by MAME's eprom screen_update and atarimo device. The stain logic restates MAME's apply_stain loop, special-priority pixels are routed the way MAME's two-pass merge handles them, and the palette output reproduces MAME's crude intensity formula exactly. Hardware-flavoured pieces (the GAL sum-of-products priority, a 74161-style TMS5220 clock counter, ADC conversion delay, shared-RAM contention/TAS handling) are real, but they sit inside a decomposition that follows MAME's functions, so the overall lean is mildly toward MAME.

findings.signal: palette intensity formula identical to MAME's approximation
findings.note: ifac = (data[15:12]+1)*(4-intensity) and r/g/b = nibble*ifac/4 copy MAME's i=((data>>12)&15)+1)*(4-m_screen_intensity) term for term. The board produces this with an analog transistor circuit, which MAME itself only approximates.

findings.signal: stain pass is MAME's apply_stain loop
findings.note: A one-flop recurrence reproduces the C loop's offnext/break behavior, including staining one pixel past the END marker. S/E are pen bit 1 / bit 2 of special (prio bit 2) pixels, the same as MAME's START_MARKER/END_MARKER masks, and the result ORs 0x400 into the colour index just as pf[x] |= 0x400 does.

findings.signal: special-priority pixels routed like MAME's two-pass merge
findings.where: rtl/core/escape_mob.v:205-228 (hit0/hit1 exclude disp_q[10]; spc_hit feeds stain)
findings.note: Pixels with priority bit 2 are written into the line buffer and then dropped from disp_valid but kept as stain markers. That copies MAME's first pass ('if (mopriority & 4) continue') followed by its separate stain pass.

findings.signal: colour-index composition follows MAME pen arithmetic
findings.note: The MO pen is built as 0x100|color<<4|pix, and the PF pen as 0x200|color<<4|pix with |0x100 for SHADE and |0x080 for M7. These are MAME's pf[x] |= 0x100 / 0x080 and mo & DATA_MASK expressions written as bit concatenations. The PFX4/5 mapping is taken from MAME's (pf>>4)&3.

findings.signal: GAL equations as literal sum-of-products with board net names
findings.note: FORCEMC0, !PF/M, M7 and SHADE are written as product-term ORs over PFX3/PFX4/PFX5/MPR0/MPR1, not as MAME's restructured if-tree, and the module ports are those GAL signals. Weakened because those equations and names are themselves in the MAME driver.

findings.signal: scan-time playfield/alpha fetch phases on pixel counter bits
findings.note: Tile RAM is read at phase 0, the graphics fetch is queued at phase 3, and the shift word is swapped at phase 7, all per 8-pixel cell during scan. This replaces tilemap callbacks with no frame/tilemap batch, but much of it is ordinary FPGA scan pipelining.

findings.signal: per-line MO build with first-writer-wins line buffers
findings.note: Each scanline reads the SLIP band link, walks the list, and blits only the matching tile row into a tagged double line buffer that refuses overwrites. MAME instead renders whole 8-line bands into a bitmap in reverse list order with overwrite. The result is the same, but the mechanism is the board's line-buffer one.

findings.signal: MO walk terminators and field extraction match atarimo config
findings.note: The link/code/x/y/width/height/prio fields use MAME's masks, the per-band start link comes from SLIP word 0x40+band, and ydiff uses MAME's negated-ypos-plus-height arithmetic. Any correct core must share this data layout.
The squeak bit loads 0101/0111 into a 4-bit counter that runs to 1111, as a 74161 with load would. MAME just recomputes a clock divisor (16 - count).

findings.signal: linear mixer gain tables match MAME's mix_w scaling
findings.note: The YM gain is 0..7 in equal steps and the TMS gain is 0,0x55,0xAA,0xFF. These are MAME's /7.0 and /3.0 linear volumes, not the board's resistor-network attenuation.

findings.signal: bus-level behavior MAME does not model
findings.note: There is DTACK wait-state generation per select, shared-RAM contention with read-modify-write locking between the two 68000s, and an ADC with a busy/EOC conversion delay. MAME uses yield() and an instant ADC read. Some of this is FPGA arbitration engineering.

The core has address-specific snoops (v_pc_seen at 0x000694, an e_flag handshake at 0x16CCD6) that gate the extra CPU's interrupt. They are tied to the game program and are evidence for neither the board nor MAME.
